 CORAM:
 THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ADITYA KUMAR  MOHAPATRA  ORDER 06.01.2026 Order No.
01. 1.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner as well as learned counsel for the State.
Perused the application as well as the prayer made therein.

3. By filing the present application under section 482 of Cr.P.C the Petitioner seeks to invoke the inherent power of this Court to quash the entire criminal proceeding in connection with C.T Case No.717 of 2014 which arises out of Bhograi P.S Case No.219 dated 27.12.2014 now pending in the file of learned Gram Nyayalaya- cum-JMFC, Bhograi which was registered for commission of an offence punishable under Section 420, 468 and 471 of the IPC.
4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner at the outset contended that the F.I.R was registered after a long gap.
He further submitted that the Petitioner was initially enlarged on anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 28.01.2015 in ABLAPL No.134 of 2015.
Thereafter, the matter was kept pending.
Finally, the Petitioner has again been noticed to appear before the learned trial court.
It was also contended that in the meantime a charge sheet has been filed and cognizance of the offence has been taken.

However, learned counsel for the Petitioner fairly submitted that no charge has been framed and that the Petitioner, who is aged about 67 years, is suffering as he is in position to appear before the court.
On such ground, learned counsel for the Petitioner contended that the continuance of the very criminal proceeding is an abuse of process of law.
Hence, it was prayed that the entire Madhusudan Ghosh vs State Of Odisha .....

criminal proceeding be quashed.

5. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand objected to the quashing of the entire criminal proceeding on the ground that a case is well made out against the Petitioner under the alleged sections.
It was contended that in the meantime the learned Magistrate has already taken cognizance.
Therefore, there exists a prima facie case against the present Petitioner.
It was also contended that at this belated stage the Petitioner cannot question the validity of the FIR which was filed more than a decade ago.
On such ground, learned counsel for the State objected to the quashing of the entire criminal proceeding.

6. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for both sides, on a careful examination of the materials on record, this Court observes that the FIR was registered in the year 2014 alleging commission of an offence punishable under Sections 420, 468 and 471 of the IPC.

On a plain reading of the FIR it is revealed that on the basis of a complaint lodged by the Assistant Registrar of the Cooperative Society, Balasore Circle alleging submission of forged Date of Birth certificate, the present criminal proceeding has been initiated.
Although more than a decade's time has elapsed in the meantime, the trial has not commenced.

Keeping in view the advanced age of the Petitioner, this Court deems it proper to dispose of the present application at this stage by granting liberty to the Petitioner to raise all the grounds at the time of framing of charge.
In such eventuality, learned trial court shall do well to consider such grounds strictly in accordance with law and shall dispose of such application by passing a reasoned order.

Further, keeping in view the fact that the case is pending for more than a decade, the learned trial court is directed to expedite the trial and to make every endeavour to conclude the same as expeditiously as possible.

Further, liberty is granted to the petitioner to move an application under Section 205 of the Cr.P.C and in such eventuality learned trial court shall consider the same strictly in accordance with law and keeping in view the fact that the case primarily involves scrutiny of documentary evidence.
8. With the aforesaid observations/ directions, the CRLMC application stands disposed of.
( Aditya Kumar Mohapatra) Judge Anil Designation: Junior Stenographer
